question: Across the episode, at which of the following moments does Sheldon appear most visibly anxious?
options: A. When he complains that the sandwich ingredients are arranged in the wrong order.
B. When Raj proposes moving the time machine between their homes every other month.
C. When Penny dismisses the time machine while criticizing the men's hobbies.
D. When he blocks Leonard from taking the boxed collectibles away to sell them.

question: At which of these separated moments does Leonard show the most intense embarrassment?
options: A. When his friends question the impulsive auction bid
B. When his time-travel joke falls flat with Penny
C. When the unexpectedly large machine is delivered
D. When he admits his worries about attracting Penny

question: Across the episode, at which moment does Howard show the most intense excitement about the time machine?
options: A. When Leonard first shows him the online time-machine auction.
B. When he examines the full-size machine in the lobby.
C. When he acts out the machine's trip into the future.
D. When he tries to buy Leonard's share of the machine.

question: How does Sheldon's visible engagement with the time machine change from the auction countdown, through seeing its actual size, to joining the play in the apartment?
options: A. He begins with mild concern, greets its full size with focused interest in the moving problem, then appears quietly satisfied but emotionally reserved during the play.
B. He begins with eager excitement, greets its full size with delighted amazement, then approaches the group's play with careful seriousness and little visible joy.
C. He begins with doubtful interest, greets its full size with amused disbelief, then joins the group's play with restrained curiosity rather than growing excitement.
D. He begins with tense curiosity, shifts into confusion and curiosity about why it would be sold, and once the group starts using it, he becomes animated and openly eager.

question: How does Leonard's visible confidence about a possible relationship with Penny change from her criticism of the group, through her later reassurance, to her departure with Mike?
options: A. He looks embarrassed but composed, remains cautious during her reassurance, then relaxes when Mike arrives and Penny leaves.
B. He looks wounded and withdrawn, briefly becomes hopeful during her reassurance, then visibly deflates and retreats to the time machine.
C. He looks irritated and defensive, grows uncomfortable as she reassures him, then returns to the time machine with renewed enthusiasm.
D. He looks quietly disappointed, becomes steadily more confident during her reassurance, then treats Mike's arrival as only a minor interruption.

question: Considering Raj's participation in the time-machine play and his later reactions while Leonard tries to sell the collection, what does Raj's nonverbal pattern most strongly suggest?
options: A. His excitement turns into bargaining focus, suggesting he mainly wants an opportunity to acquire the rare items cheaply.
B. His playfulness turns into protective alarm, suggesting the memorabilia matters to him emotionally rather than only as property.
C. His amusement turns into concern for Leonard, suggesting he mainly wants to protect his friend's freedom to choose.
D. His competitive energy turns into caution, suggesting he mainly wants to prevent the friends from fighting over the collection.
